root.name: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Three Knights Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Nf3

overview: White develops the knight instead of Qc2 or e3, keeping options open. Black chooses ...O-O, ...c5 or ...b6; typical play is e3, Bd3, O-O against doubled c-pawns or the bishop pair. Positions are strategic with Black fighting for e4 and White for the centre.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with e3, Bd3, O-O and d5/e4 central play, or Qc2 to recapture on c3 without doubling.
Seek the bishop pair if Black captures on c3, and use the centre.

black_ideas.idea: Pin Nc3, control e4, castle and take on c3 to ruin White's pawns.
Hit the centre with ...c5 or ...d5, or play ...b6 and ...Bb7.

typical_structures.structure: Doubled c-pawns for White against the bishop pair.
Hanging pawns or IQP after ...c5 and ...d5.

character.notes: Strategic, with a tense centre; few forced lines compared with the main Nimzo lines.

structure.notes: Centre in tension; flexible with doubled pawns options.

level.notes: Strategic piece play and structure judgement more than memorisation.

character.reason: Strategic and flexible without forced sharp lines.

soundness.reason: Main line with a long pedigree.

structure.reason: Centre in tension, with pawn structure decided by later exchanges.

level.reason: Strategic ideas matter more than forced lines.

plans.reason: Black trades on c3 for White's structure.
